facts.raw_span: intensely pruritic skin lesions on her anterior thighs
lesions first appeared 2 weeks earlier in recurrent 3‐day outbreaks
well‐defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology
central clearing, and purpuric edges
symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs in a mirror‐image pattern
no systemic symptoms
no preceding infection, topical exposures, sunburn, bites, animal contacts, or recent medications
laboratory studies were within normal limits

complete blood count, biochemistry, urinalysis, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C‐reactive protein, complement levels (C3, C4, C1q), immunoglobulin levels, rheumatoid factor, and acute‐phase reactants were within normal limits
Antinuclear, anti–double‐stranded DNA, antineutrophil cytoplasmic, anti–Ro, anti–La, and transglutaminase antibodies were negative
Serologies for syphilis, hepatitis B and C viruses, HIV, cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, and parvovirus B19 were negative
A chest radiograph was unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient's skin lesions with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, central clearing, and purpuric edges are characteristic of erythema multiforme.
The patient's intensely pruritic skin lesions with recurrent 3-day outbreaks are consistent with urticaria.
The patient's symmetrically distributed skin lesions on the anterior thighs could be due to contact dermatitis.
The patient's skin lesions with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology are also seen in pityriasis rosea.
The patient's recurrent skin lesions could be due to a viral exanthem, although serologies were negative.
The patient's skin lesions with purpuric edges could be due to an autoimmune bullous disease, although autoantibodies were negative.
The patient's skin lesions with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology are also seen in psoriasis.
The patient's skin lesions with purpuric edges could be due to lichen planus.

rationales.F01: The presence of intensely pruritic skin lesions is more typical of urticaria and contact dermatitis, but also seen in erythema multiforme.
rationales.F03: The description of well-defined, confluent, erythematous papules and plaques with annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology is highly suggestive of erythema multiforme.
rationales.F04: The presence of central clearing and purpuric edges is highly characteristic of erythema multiforme.
rationales.F10: The absence of antinuclear and other autoantibodies makes autoimmune bullous disease less likely.
rationales.F11: The negative serologies for various viruses reduce the likelihood of viral exanthem.
